synthetic_unknown_surrogate_generator.motivation: DQNGuard performance appears strongly dependent on surrogate direction/geometry. A learned generator could synthesize pseudo-unknown RF examples from known-only data, providing a task-specific surrogate class for DQN calibration without consuming true unknown target data.
concept: Train an autoencoder/generative model only on allowed known/surrogate-side data.
Generate synthetic signals or latent perturbations intended to behave like useful pseudo-unknowns.
Define a surrogate-quality objective from measurable properties that correlate with strong real surrogate directions, rather than using target unknown labels.
Use the generated pseudo-unknown class to tune/train the DQNGuard rejector while preserving the target-unknown firewall.
synthetic_unknown_surrogate_generator.key_research_question: Identify which observable surrogate properties predict strong DQNGuard unknown detection, then optimize a generator toward those properties.

calibration rejection behavior under known-only constraints
directional surrogate effectiveness learned from training folds only
synthetic_unknown_surrogate_generator.core_challenge: A universal generator may leak information or fail to generalize across leave-one/leave-two-out unknown folds. A strict design may require one generator per training fold/unknown holdout configuration, or a conditional generator trained without access to the held-out unknown.
scientific_constraints: No true held-out unknown data for generator tuning or model selection.
No target-test labels before final scoring.
Generator selection criteria must be frozen using training-fold information only.

Compare against deterministic real-surrogate picker and existing DQNGuard/VarMax/DQN-IDS baselines.
